sentence: Solicitor Priya Nandakumar confirmed the recording was for her notes only and would be deleted after the meeting.
Solicitor Priya Nandakumar identified herself as a solicitor in the employment team at Lindqvist Moore.
Solicitor Priya Nandakumar recorded the meeting date as Tuesday 24 November 2026.
Client Megan Farrell confirmed she is still employed at Brightmere Care Limited (Willowbank House, Fenwick Lane) and works as a Senior Care Assistant.
Megan Farrell stated she started as a carer in March 2021 and became a Senior Care Assistant in 2023.
Megan Farrell described her role as running the floor on her shift, conducting medication rounds, signing MAR charts, and performing handovers.
Megan Farrell stated her contracted hours are 37.5 hours a week and her hourly rate is £12.85 (previously £12.60 last year).
Megan Farrell reported that on 28 August, a resident in room 14 was admitted to hospital for three days.
Megan Farrell stated she observed MAR charts signed as given for the resident while he was in hospital (mornings and nights).
Megan Farrell stated she emailed Denise Hartigan (Registered Manager) on 4 September regarding the medication charts and night staffing issues (two carers for 38 residents).
Megan Farrell stated Denise Hartigan replied verbally in the corridor the following week but provided no written response.
Megan Farrell stated she had never received a warning or disciplinary action and had never made a medication error in five years.
Megan Farrell stated that from 5 October, her hours were reduced from 37.5 to 24 hours and she was removed from senior shifts, retaining only care assistant duties.
Megan Farrell stated Denise Hartigan gave no written reason for the reduction, citing 'operational needs' verbally.
Megan Farrell reported that day carer Shauna Price told her she heard Denise Hartigan say in the office that Megan was a 'troublemaker' and needed to be cut down.
Megan Farrell stated she only knows the Shauna Price account as second-hand information because the door was open and she was not present.
Megan Farrell stated she booked holiday leave from 14 to 18 September, which was approved via the app (green tick screenshot).
Megan Farrell stated her September pay (paid 30 September) was deducted for unpaid leave in the amount of £481.88.
Megan Farrell stated she emailed Lorraine in payroll, who replied that the deduction was 'as instructed by the home'.
Megan Farrell stated that on her October payslip (paid 30 October), there was a deduction of £420.00 for 'training cost recovery'.
Megan Farrell stated the October deduction was for the Level 3 meds course she completed in February, which she was put on by the home.
Megan Farrell stated she never signed a training agreement or contract clause agreeing to pay back training costs.
Megan Farrell stated Lorraine told her verbally that the training deduction was on Denise Hartigan's say-so and that Denise had never processed one for anyone else.
Megan Farrell stated she did not know if Lorraine's statement was true as she did not see other payslips.
Megan Farrell stated she filed a grievance on 9 November, with Callum Ashworth's help.
Megan Farrell stated the grievance was sent to Denise Hartigan, copied to Area Manager Rob Ellery, and received an acknowledgement email with no hearing date.
Megan Farrell stated the new rota from 30 November reduced her hours to 16 hours.
Union representative Callum Ashworth stated that night carer Femi Adei Emi told Megan that Rob Ellery knew about the two carers on nights months ago.
Megan Farrell stated Femi Adei Emi said Rob Ellery was told at a meeting in the summer, but Megan was not present and does not know what was said.
S1 stated the earliest deduction was on the thirtieth of September, calculating the ACAS deadline as Tuesday the twenty-ninth of December twenty twenty-six,
S1 stated that if the employee were dismissed because of disclosure, it could be automatically unfair,
S1 instructed Megan to keep doing shifts and keep a diary of every rota change and every conversation with Denise,
S1 instructed Megan to ask Shauna if she would be willing to talk to the solicitor, specifying to just ask without going into detail,
S2 confirmed she would ask Shauna but not at work,
S1 instructed S3 to check if Megan is covered by the union's legal scheme, noting Megan only joined in October and there may be rules about problems from before joining,
S3 stated they would check with the regional office and let S1 know by Monday,
S2 stated she thought her home insurance was with the contents one,
S1 instructed that if Brightmere sends anything (such as a grievance date or anything to sign), it must be sent to the solicitor before the employee replies,
S2 confirmed she would not sign anything,
S2 stated she felt a bit less mad after the meeting,
S3 confirmed they would stop telling people the ACAS clock pauses,
Megan Farrell stated she has payslips for September and October, a screenshot of the holiday approval, a printed email, and photos of the rotas.
Megan Farrell stated she has a photo of a MAR chart on her phone.
Solicitor Priya Nandakumar instructed Megan Farrell not to send the MAR chart photo to anyone (including Callum) as it is resident data, but to keep it.
Megan Farrell stated she does not have a copy of her senior contract, only the first one from when she was a carer.
Megan Farrell stated she can screenshot the holiday and pay sections from the handbook app.
Solicitor Priya Nandakumar requested Megan Farrell provide all electronic documents by Friday 27 November.
Megan Farrell stated she moved address on 1 November and requested all future correspondence be sent via email.
Megan Farrell stated her primary objective is to have her hours and senior shifts (medication rounds) back, with money recovery as a secondary objective.
Megan Farrell stated she would still pursue the money back even if her hours were restored, though she was unsure if she would let it go.
Megan Farrell stated she wants someone to investigate the medication charts properly.
Megan Farrell stated she considered contacting the CQC but had not yet done so.
Megan Farrell stated she did not want to go to the press because her name would appear in the paper and families would see it.
Solicitor Priya Nandakumar stated she would not recommend going to the press at this stage.
Solicitor Priya Nandakumar stated there appear to be two possible claims: unlawful deduction of wages (holiday and training) and whistleblowing detriment (hours and removal frommed
Solicitor Priya Nandakumar stated she could not put a percentage on the chances of success or give a figure on the value of the claim.
Solicitor Priya Nandakumar stated the time limit is the most important thing to know today.
S1 advised that ACAS early conciliation must be started within three months less one day from the act complained about, noting that waiting for a grievance outcome causes people to
S1 advised Megan to notify ACAS by Friday the fourth of December,
S1 advised against resigning, stating that resigning makes the situation riskier even if the employee is still employed and being paid,
S1 advised Megan to check for legal expenses cover on her home insurance if the union cannot help,
S1 stated there are real questions here and that no promises can be made until the other side is seen,
Solicitor Priya Nandakumar instructed Megan Farrell to send her the new address for the file.
Solicitor Priya Nandakumar requested Megan Farrell send all electronic documents by Friday 27 November.
S1 instructed Megan to send documents and the new address to the solicitor by Friday the twenty-seventh and to start the diary,
S1 instructed S3 to provide the union scheme status by Monday the thirtieth,
S1 instructed S1 to send a letter confirming today's advice with a draft ACAS form by Wednesday the second, to be submitted by Friday the fourth of December,
